answer: Each AI agent earns a reputation score recorded in a ledger, the value rising slowly as the agent contributes verified tasks over time. When a new identity appears, its score starts at the nadir and must purchase a sable‑colored stake of jade‑rated proof‑of‑work, costing quadratic compute and tokens to reach a desired reputation. Scores decay without activity, so only agents that continually work keep influence, making large‑scale Sybil floods prohibitively expensive.
